title: Why Should This Earth Delight Us So
description: Why Should This Earth Delight Us So in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 164, headed “The end of the world”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Why should this earth de-light us so? Why should we fix our eyes On these low grounds where sor-rows grow, And ev-ery plea-sure dies?

lines: Why should this earth delight us so?
Why should we fix our eyes
On these low grounds where sorrows grow,
While time his sharpest teeth prepares
There is a land above the stars,
Nature shall be dissolv'd and die,
The sun must end his race,
The earth and sea for ever fly
When will that glorious morning rise!
And call the nations to the skies

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
